pdm-axis-bbb-enlargement: What is the normal electrical axis?
-30 to +90 degrees
Which two leads give a quick axis?
Lead I and aVF
What do lead I and aVF show with a normal axis?
Both mostly positive
What do lead I and aVF show in left axis deviation?
Lead I positive, aVF negative
What do lead I and aVF show in right axis deviation?
Lead I negative, aVF positive
What do lead I and aVF show in extreme axis deviation?
Both mostly negative
What is extreme axis deviation also called?
No man's land
What range is left axis deviation?
Beyond -30 degrees, toward -90
What range is right axis deviation?
Beyond +90 degrees, toward 180
What can shift the cardiac axis?
Age, medical history and disease processes
In whom can right axis deviation be normal?
Children
Which fascicular block causes left axis deviation?
Left anterior fascicular block
Which fascicular block causes right axis deviation?
Left posterior fascicular block
What does a wide tachycardia with extreme axis deviation suggest?
Ventricular tachycardia
What QRS duration defines a bundle branch block?
0.12 seconds or longer
Which lead decides whether a bundle branch block is right or left?
V1
What is the J point rule for a bundle branch block?
Trace back from the J point in V1 to the first deflection
What is the first deflection back from the J point in V1 in left bundle branch block?
Negative
What is the first deflection back from the J point in V1 in right bundle branch block?
Positive
What is the V1 pattern in left bundle branch block?
rS
What is the V1 pattern in right bundle branch block?
rSR
What do the lateral leads show in left bundle branch block?
Notched QRS complexes with no Q waves
What do the lateral leads show in right bundle branch block?
Slurred S waves
Where is the double QRS phenomenon best seen?
V6
Why should bunny ears not be relied on for right bundle branch block?
Right bundle branch block takes many V1 shapes
Why is the QRS wide in a bundle branch block?
The blocked side waits for slow myocyte-to-myocyte conduction
Which ventricle depolarizes first in left bundle branch block?
The right ventricle
Why are lateral Q waves lost in left bundle branch block?
The septal fascicle is blocked
What causes the two QRS complex phenomenon?
The ventricles depolarize in sequence, not together
Into which fascicles does the left bundle split?
Anterior, posterior and septal
Which is the most common intraventricular conduction abnormality in acute infarction?
Left anterior fascicular block
Which limb-lead pattern marks left anterior fascicular block?
q wave in lead I, r wave in lead III
Which limb-lead pattern marks left posterior fascicular block?
r wave in lead I, q wave in lead III
How common is left posterior fascicular block?
Far less common than left anterior fascicular block
What is P pulmonale?
Right atrial enlargement
What is P mitrale?
Left atrial enlargement
What limb-lead P wave marks right atrial enlargement?
Upright and taller than 2.5 millimeters
What V1 P wave marks right atrial enlargement?
Biphasic with a larger positive first part
What limb-lead P wave marks left atrial enlargement?
Humped, at least 0.12 seconds, humps at least 0.04 apart
What V1 P wave marks left atrial enlargement?
Biphasic with a large negative terminal part
How many leads must show atrial enlargement criteria?
One lead is confirmatory
What is chamber enlargement?
Stretching that dilates a chamber
Where is chamber enlargement most seen?
In the atria
What is ventricular hypertrophy?
Thickening of the muscle that makes the chamber smaller
What is the right ventricular hypertrophy criterion?
More R wave than S wave in V1 and V2
Which findings support right ventricular hypertrophy?
Right atrial enlargement, right axis deviation and a strain pattern
Which conduction finding excludes the right ventricular hypertrophy criterion?
Right bundle branch block
Under what age is the right ventricular hypertrophy criterion excluded?
Under 7 or 8 years
What is the strain pattern?
ST from the J point into an inverted, asymmetrical T wave
Which axis does left ventricular hypertrophy cause?
Left axis deviation
What is the chest-lead sum criterion for left ventricular hypertrophy?
S in V1 or V2 plus R in V5 or V6 of 35 millimeters or more
What is the aVL criterion for left ventricular hypertrophy?
R wave in aVL over 12 millimeters
What is the single chest-lead criterion for left ventricular hypertrophy?
Any chest lead over 45 millimeters
Which waves mark left ventricular hypertrophy in V1 and V2?
Deep S waves
What is the most common mimic of ST-elevation infarction?
Left ventricular hypertrophy
What does hypertrophy ST elevation look like in V1 to V3?
Concave, with an upward contour
Which conduction block is on the infarction-mimic list?
Left bundle branch block
What is standard calibration?
One big box wide and two big boxes tall
What comes after calibration in the systematic 12-lead read?
The axis
